title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 172
paragraphs: Next after these Auschisae, moving westward, come the Nasamones, a numerous people, who in summer leave their flocks by the sea and go up to the region of Augila to gather the fruit of the date-palms, which grow there in great numbers, very large, and all fruit-bearing. They hunt the wingless locusts, dry them in the sun, grind them up, and then sprinkle them onto milk and drink it. Their custom is for each man to have many wives, and they share them in much the same way as the Massagetae—that is, they set up a staff in front of the door and so have intercourse. When a Nasamonian man marries his first wife, the custom is for the bride on the first night to go through the whole company of guests and have intercourse with them, and each man when he has lain with her gives a gift—whatever he has brought with him from his house. Their forms of oath and of divination are as follows. They swear by the men of their own people who are reported to have been most upright and brave, laying their hands on these men's tombs; and they practice divination by going to the burial mounds of their ancestors and lying down to sleep upon them after praying—and whatever thing the man sees in his dream, that he accepts. They also practice the exchange of pledges in this way: one gives the other to drink from his hand, and drinks himself from the other's hand; and if they have no liquid, they take dust from the ground and lick it.
